title: DSM-5 Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Criteria
source: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5)
note: Symptoms must be present in early developmental period and cause clinically significant impairment

A.title: Persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts
A.requirement: Must meet ALL three subcriteria (A1, A2, A3)

A1.title: Deficits in social-emotional reciprocity
A1.description: Ranging from abnormal social approach and failure of normal back-and-forth conversation; to reduced sharing of interests, emotions, or affect; to failure to initiate or respond to social interactions
exemplars: Reduced sharing of emotions or affect
Failure to respond to social interactions
toddler_indicators: Does not respond to name when called
Does not share enjoyment or interests with others
Does not seek attention from caregivers
Limited social smiling or emotional expression
Does not imitate others' actions
Does not look to caregiver for reaction in new situations

A2.title: Deficits in nonverbal communicative behaviors used for social interaction
A2.description: Ranging from poorly integrated verbal and nonverbal communication; to abnormalities in eye contact and body language or deficits in understanding and use of gestures; to a total lack of facial expressions and nonverbal communication
exemplars: Poorly integrated verbal and nonverbal communication
toddler_indicators: Limited or unusual eye contact
Does not follow pointing or gaze
Does not point to share interest
Does not use gestures to communicate
Limited facial expressions during interactions

A3.title: Deficits in developing, maintaining, and understanding relationships
A3.description: Ranging from difficulties adjusting behavior to suit various social contexts; to difficulties in sharing imaginative play or in making friends; to absence of interest in peers
exemplars: Difficulties adjusting behavior to social contexts
toddler_indicators: Limited interest in other children
Does not engage in pretend play
Prefers to play alone
Does not imitate social play

B.title: Restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities
B.requirement: Must meet at least TWO of four subcriteria (B1, B2, B3, B4)

B1.title: Stereotyped or repetitive motor movements, use of objects, or speech
B1.description: Such as simple motor stereotypies, lining up toys or flipping objects, echolalia, idiosyncratic phrases
exemplars: Simple motor stereotypies (hand flapping, finger flicking)
toddler_indicators: Unusual finger movements near eyes
Lines up toys instead of playing with them
Spins wheels or other object parts repeatedly
Flaps hands when excited or upset
Rocks body back and forth

B2.title: Insistence on sameness, inflexible adherence to routines, or ritualized patterns
B2.description: Such as extreme distress at small changes, difficulties with transitions, rigid thinking patterns, greeting rituals, need to take same route or eat same food every day
exemplars: Need for same food every day
toddler_indicators: Extreme distress with minor changes in routine
Insists on specific rituals
Difficulty transitioning between activities

B3.title: Highly restricted, fixated interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus
B3.description: Such as strong attachment to or preoccupation with unusual objects, excessively circumscribed or perseverative interests
toddler_indicators: Unusual attachment to specific objects
Fixated on specific topics or activities
Intense focus on parts of objects

B4.title: Hyper- or hyporeactivity to sensory input or unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment
B4.description: Such as apparent indifference to pain/temperature, adverse response to specific sounds or textures, excessive smelling or touching of objects, visual fascination with lights or movement
exemplars: Visual fascination with lights or movement
toddler_indicators: Upset by everyday sounds (vacuum, blender)
Unusual response to textures
Fascination with lights or spinning objects
Avoids or seeks specific sensory input
Unusual reaction to movement activities

C.title: Symptoms present in early developmental period
C.description: Symptoms must be present in the early developmental period (but may not become fully manifest until social demands exceed limited capacities, or may be masked by learned strategies in later life)

D.title: Clinically significant impairment
D.description: Symptoms cause clinically significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of current functioning

E.title: Not better explained by intellectual disability
E.description: These disturbances are not better explained by intellectual disability (intellectual developmental disorder) or global developmental delay. Intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder frequently co-occur; to make comorbid diagnoses of autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability, social communication should be below that expected for general developmental level

level_1.title: Level 1: Requiring Support
level_1.social_communication: Without supports in place, deficits in social communication cause noticeable impairments. Difficulty initiating social interactions, and clear examples of atypical or unsuccessful responses to social overtures of others. May appear to have decreased interest in social interactions.
level_1.restricted_behaviors: Inflexibility of behavior causes significant interference with functioning in one or more contexts. Difficulty switching between activities. Problems of organization and planning hamper independence.

level_2.title: Level 2: Requiring Substantial Support
level_2.social_communication: Marked deficits in verbal and nonverbal social communication skills; social impairments apparent even with supports in place; limited initiation of social interactions; and reduced or abnormal responses to social overtures from others.
level_2.restricted_behaviors: Inflexibility of behavior, difficulty coping with change, or other restricted/repetitive behaviors appear frequently enough to be obvious to the casual observer and interfere with functioning in a variety of contexts. Distress and/or difficulty changing focus or action.

level_3.title: Level 3: Requiring Very Substantial Support
level_3.social_communication: Severe deficits in verbal and nonverbal social communication skills cause severe impairments in functioning, very limited initiation of social interactions, and minimal response to social overtures from others.
level_3.restricted_behaviors: Inflexibility of behavior, extreme difficulty coping with change, or other restricted/repetitive behaviors markedly interfere with functioning in all spheres. Great distress/difficulty changing focus or action.
